title: The smallest country
body: Vatican City is the smallest country in the world, with less than half a square kilometre of land and fewer than 1,000 people.

title: A country with 11 time zones
body: Russia is so wide that it spans 11 time zones. When it is morning in one end, it can be night in the other.

title: Everest is still growing
body: Mount Everest is 8,849 metres high. The tectonic plates under it keep pushing, so the mountain grows by a few millimetres every year.

title: Antarctica is a desert
body: A desert is a place with very little rain or snow, and Antarctica receives so little that it counts as the largest desert on Earth. It is also the coldest, windiest and driest continent.

title: The deepest place in the ocean
body: The Mariana Trench in the Pacific Ocean is nearly 11 kilometres deep. If Mount Everest were put in it, the peak would still be under more than 2 kilometres of water.

title: The sea you can float on
body: The Dead Sea, between Jordan and Israel, is so salty that people float easily on top of it. Its shore is the lowest dry land on Earth.

title: A country that is also a continent
body: Australia is both a country and a continent, the only one in the world that is both.

title: The great river debate
body: The Nile and the Amazon both claim to be the longest river in the world. Measurements differ depending on where each river is said to start, so scientists still disagree.

title: Why seasons happen
body: The Earth is tilted. When the northern half leans toward the Sun it is summer there and winter in the south. Near the Equator, as in Uganda, the seasons are mostly about rain, not temperature.

title: Most of the Earth is ocean
body: About 71% of the Earth’s surface is covered by ocean, but humans have explored only a small part of it.

title: The driest and the wettest
body: The Atacama Desert in Chile has places where it has hardly ever rained. Others, like parts of north-east India, get more than ten metres of rain each year.
